intervals.label: approved by the LSC
intervals.quote: The experiment was approved by the LSC at the beginning of 2017.

intervals.label: installation in Hall A of the LSC
intervals.note: The J. Instrum. paper (arXiv:2312.12622) says the installation was carried out at the end of 2018 and the Eur. Phys. J. C paper (arXiv:1812.04519) that the whole detector was moved underground in 2018.
intervals.quote: During 2017 into 2018 the experiment was installed at the hall A of LSC.

intervals.label: commissioning and first engineering runs in Hall A
intervals.note: Year precision; the end is the start of the 2019 data-taking campaigns.
intervals.quote: End of 2018 the experiment has started its first engineering runs at low pressure, and it faces the first physics runs for 2019.

intervals.label: data-taking campaigns in Hall A
intervals.note: Neon + 2% isobutane at 4 bar from 2019; argon + 1% isobutane at 1.5 bar at the end of 2018. The end is the dismounting in October 2022.

intervals.label: dismounted at the request of the LSC and re-installed in Lab2500
intervals.note: The paper says the experiment was re-installed in the Lab2500 at LSC in spring 2023 and has been taking data from July 2023; the end of this interval is that July 2023 restart.
intervals.quote: In October 2022, when the parts with surface contamination were going to be replaced, the experiment was completely dismounted after the request of the LSC management

intervals.label: data taking in Lab2500
intervals.note: Latest evidence of operation: arXiv:2510.05877 (October 2025) reports a 37Ar calibration measurement in the detector at the LSC. No source gives a later date or an end of data taking; status as of 2026-10-26 is inferred, not confirmed.
intervals.quote: the detector has been taking data, from July 2023

placements.note: Hall A of the LSC from the installation (2018) to October 2022, then Lab2500 from spring 2023 (arXiv:2312.12622); the site record covers the whole Canfranc laboratory.
placements.quote: During 2017 into 2018 the experiment was installed at the hall A of LSC.

active_mass.display: 0.30 kg of Ar (0.16 kg of Ne)
active_mass.note: At up to 10 bar; operated at 1.5 to 4 bar so far.
active_mass.quote: 20 l of pressurized gas up to 10 bar, corresponding to 0.30 kg of Ar or 0.16 kg of Ne

depth.quote: The present TREX-DM set-up installed at the hall A of the Canfranc laboratory, placed at a depth of 2450 m.w.e.

instrumented_volume.quote: 20 l of pressurized gas up to 10 bar

summary.plain: A cylindrical copper vessel of gas (neon or argon with a little isobutane) with two Micromegas readout planes that image the tracks of tiny nuclear recoils, inside lead and copper shielding.
summary.technical: Two side-by-side common-cathode TPC modules, a 0.5 m diameter, 0.5 m long copper vessel 6 cm thick, Teflon field cage with Kapton copper-strip shaping rings, aluminised Mylar cathode, X-Y strips of 1 mm pitch on 25x25 cm^2 microbulk Micromegas (official TREX-DM page).

technology.quote: TREX-DM (TPC for Rare Event eXperiments - Dark Matter) [2] is a Micromegas-read High Pressure TPC
technology.value: High-pressure gas time projection chamber with microbulk Micromegas readout
